title: Unconstrained quadratic model with a full set of points

origin.description: Minimize a function of several variables by a trust-region method. The Fortran code chooses the full quadratic interpolation set itself.

arguments.name: par
arguments.text: Numeric starting values. Every value must be finite.

arguments.name: fn
arguments.text: Objective. Its first argument is the parameter vector, and it must return one number.

arguments.name: control
arguments.text: rhobeg, rhoend, iprint, and maxfun. npt is still accepted and may warn, but the search does not use it.

origin.details: rhobeg defaults to min(0.95, 0.2 * max(abs(par))) and rhoend to 1e-6 times rhobeg. The Fortran routine sets its own interpolation count, (n^2 + 3n + 2) / 2.
origin.value: A list with par, fval, feval, ierr, and msg. ierr 0 is a normal exit. 1 means maxfun was hit. 3 is a trust-region step that did not reduce the model.

translation.description: The same control checks. The search is the uobyqa crate, a port of Powell's Fortran. npt is not passed in.

arguments.name: par
arguments.text: Starting values. A number or a sequence of numbers.

arguments.name: fn
arguments.text: Objective. The first argument is the parameter list.

arguments.name: control
arguments.text: Dict of rhobeg, rhoend, iprint, and maxfun. npt is accepted and may warn, then ignored.

translation.details: The crate returns Powell's Fortran ierr. This wrapper remaps 390 to 1 and 2101 to 3. fval is a fresh call at the returned point and is not included in feval.
translation.value: MinqaResult with par, fval, feval, ierr, msg, and classes ("uobyqa", "minqa").
translation.example:
from minqa import uobyqa

def fr(x):
    return 100 * (x[1] - x[0] ** 2) ** 2 + (1 - x[0]) ** 2

print(uobyqa([1, 2], fr))

name: uobyqa
